About us
Owner, Boesman
Boesman has a passion for nature since childhood, however he studied to be a teacher but later worked as an insurance broker. He was not happy with earning such huge amount of money, led him to leave it all and get back to nature. There he was named "Boesman ( Afrikaans word for Bushman )" by his boss because left everything just to get back to nature...
Sossus on foot
The company "Sossus on foot" was founded in 1996 as the guiding company in Sossusvlei. Boesman started a transfer service for the last 5km where 4x4 vehicles are essential. Later he was joined by Frans Kasera and an ex Japanese volunteer, Yuri who became Boesman's wife later. Then we started to offer Guided Walks in Sossusvlei in 1999. Although "Guided Walks" became very popular with tourists visiting Sossusvlei, because of changes in government legislation, we moved out. We then started to offer Desert Tours on our own property, "Desert Farm Cha-re".
Bushman's Desert Camp, Farm Cha-re
In the old days, the farm Cha-re was used for Karakul sheep farming. Although the farm was too harsh to continue their farming, this was perfect place for us to introduce the Namib Desert to our guests. It has got dunes, plains, mountains, canyons, sand stone mountains... all sorts of the Namib Desert.
As the guests who join our Desert Tour required a place to overnight, we first established campsites and then later built self-catering units with an open air concept. We have 12stunning en-suite rooms with fully opening sliding doors in front and big windows on one side, which will give you the feeling of being part of nature.

Where to find us?
Farm Cha-re is 113km from Sesriem which is the entrance to Sossusvlei and 33km north of Solitaire on C14 ( which leads to Walvis bay/Swakopmund ). There you will see a sign post with shoes hanging from it. Turn at the "shoes" 2km further in you will find the camp.

Self-catering Rooms | Bushman's Desert Camp/Sossus on foot
top of page
Self-catering Rooms
A stunning desert setting, surrounded by breathtaking views
Scenic setting...
Beautiful landscapes surrounded by the timeless sandstone formations of the ancient Namib Desert.
Private verandah with views
Spacious rooms featuring large windows and breathtaking views start your day with a peaceful morning coffee on your private verandah!
Rustic
Charming rustic self-catering units equipped with all the essentials, including cutlery and barbecue facilities for a true desert escape.
Spacious and comfortable
Comfortable twin beds with bedding provided, along with triple and double room options to suit your stay.
All you need...
Each room includes a shaded carport, a solar-heated hot shower, and a 220V power point for your comfort. While there's no WiFi, it's a chance to unwind and enjoy a more unplugged getaway!
Gathering
Perfect for bringing family and friends together, creating special moments, and making lasting memories.
Meal options
Barbecue packs and firewood are available to make your outdoor cooking effortless. Treat yourself to fresh garden salads and garlic bread for dinner, or enjoy coffee and rusks to start your day. Simply inquire when booking to plan your meals!
For a special time...
The Japanese Kitchen is open for December holidays and select weekends. Please inquire about availability when booking.
Swimming pool
A small swimming pool, perfect for cooling off on a warm afternoon, is available as a shared facility for both self-catering rooms and campsites.
For the thirst...
A charming and cozy bar awaits for your relaxed afternoons, serving as a shared facility for both self-catering rooms and campsites.
12 en-suit self-catering units with the views
Each unit features a private verandah with barbecue facilities, along with basic amenities such as cutlery, plates, a kettle, pots, and a gas burner. You'll also find 220V power points, a shaded carport, and a solar-heated warm shower. While MTC connection is available at the central reception area, there's no Wi-Fi offering you the perfect opportunity to unplug and reconnect with the serene surroundings...
